meta.title: What Did Ancient Humans Actually Do All Day?
meta.working_title: They Found Food in 15 Hours a Week. Where Did Your Time Go?
meta.device: A running 'HOURS THAT ARE YOURS' clock in the corner: it shows a full free afternoon for the hunter-gatherer, then shrinks act by act as farming arrives, ending on the viewer's alarm.
meta.style: Calm serious documentary. Warm firelight palette for the camp, cold blue-grey for the modern office and the alarm. Painted savanna and Kalahari plates, parchment maps, 3D props (spear, hide, skeleton bones, shell beads, flute, plough, grain sacks, alarm clock).

shots.vo: This morning, a machine screamed at you until you got up.
shots.visual: Dark bedroom, phone alarm lights up a sleeping face; the screen reads 6:00. Cold blue light.
shots.anim: Dark, cold blue room. Phone screen flashes on the alarm beat (SFX alarm), slow push-in on the sleeping face; eyes snap open on 'screamed'.

shots.vo: You silenced it, and from that second the day was already spoken for. Where to be. What to finish. How many hours belong to someone else.
shots.visual: Modern figure sits up, rubs eyes; a calendar fills with blocks behind him, one by one, on each phrase.
shots.anim: He sits up and rubs his eyes (2-beat arm move). Calendar blocks pop in one per phrase: 'where to be', 'what to finish', 'whose hours'.

shots.vo: Now go back fifty thousand years.
shots.visual: Hard cut: the calendar dissolves into dawn mist over an African savanna camp; painted golden light.
shots.anim: Calendar dissolves into dawn mist (0.8 s cross-dissolve). Slow pull-back reveals the camp; mist layers drift at different speeds (parallax).

shots.vo: A man wakes with the light. No alarm, no shift, no one waiting for him.
shots.visual: Hunter-gatherer wakes beside a smouldering fire, stretches slowly; birds cross the sky.
shots.anim: He rises from the hides and stretches, arms up, eased; birds cross the sky; the fire smoulders and smoke curls.

shots.vo: He owns a spear, two hides and a fire. And he gets to ask a question most of us never get to ask on a weekday morning.
shots.visual: Push in on his face; 3D props pop around him: spear, two hides, embers.
shots.anim: Push-in to medium close. The spear, hides and fire pop in around him with a small overshoot, each on its word.

shots.vo: What do I feel like doing today?
shots.visual: Handwritten callout card, rotated -4 degrees, over the camp.
shots.anim: Handwritten card scales in at -4 degrees beside him as he looks out across the plain; a soft hold.

shots.vo: Your brain is already pushing back. Ancient life was short, brutal and hungry, wasn't it? Every hour a fight to stay alive.
shots.visual: Old textbook illustration style: a desperate caveman fighting a beast, stamped 'THE OFFICIAL STORY'.
shots.anim: Old textbook-print look (halftone). A caveman fights a beast in a frozen illustration; 'THE OFFICIAL STORY' stamp slams in (SFX stamp).

shots.vo: For a long time, that was the version in every textbook. Then scientists started counting, and digging, and the story cracked.
shots.visual: The textbook page tears; behind it, an excavation trench with string grid lines.
shots.anim: The textbook page tears down the middle (paper SFX) and the camera pushes through into an excavation trench with string grid lines.

shots.vo: Which leaves a strange question. You live surrounded by machines built to save time. Washing machines, microwaves, cars.
shots.visual: Modern kitchen; each machine pops in as named, with a small 'TIME SAVED' tag.
shots.anim: Each machine pops in as it is named, a small 'TIME SAVED' tag swinging on each; the worker looks from one to the next.

shots.vo: So how did people with none of that end up with more free afternoons than you? And where did your hours go?
shots.visual: Split frame: hunter resting by the fire on the left, office worker at a desk on the right. Hours clock appears top left.
shots.anim: Split frame wipes in from the centre line. Left side warm and moving (fire, breathing); right side cold and still. The hours clock appears top left.

shots.visual: Title card over a painted fire at dusk.
shots.onscreen: WHAT DID ANCIENT HUMANS DO ALL DAY?
shots.anim: Title scales in with a slight overshoot over the dusk fire; embers float upward; whoosh + low drum hit.

shots.vo: The first clue comes out of the ground in the Middle East, the Levant and Anatolia, where some of the earliest farms began.
shots.visual: Parchment map of the eastern Mediterranean; the Levant and Anatolia glow; a dig marker drops.
shots.anim: Parchment map; the Levant and Anatolia glow in turn, a dig-site pin drops in with a bounce.

shots.vo: Over decades, archaeologists dug up skeletons from people who lived in the same region a few thousand years apart.
shots.visual: Excavation pit at dusk, lanterns, brushes; two outlined skeletons side by side in the soil.
shots.anim: Lanterns flicker; brushes sweep soil away to reveal two outlined skeletons; slow push.

shots.vo: The first set of bones is tall and thick. The teeth are worn, but nearly free of decay. The joints are clean.
shots.visual: 3D skeleton A rotates slowly on a lab table; labels point to long bones, teeth, joints.
shots.anim: Skeleton A rotates slowly (3D prop). Labels draw on with lines to bones, teeth, joints as each is named.

shots.vo: The second tells a harder story. Teeth full of cavities. A spine worn by the same motion, repeated thousands of times. A shorter life.
shots.visual: 3D skeleton B beside it, shorter; red highlights on teeth, lower spine, knees.
shots.anim: Skeleton B slides in beside A, shorter. Red highlights pulse on teeth, then spine, then knees, in time with the words.

shots.vo: One was a hunter-gatherer. One was an early farmer. Take a guess.
shots.visual: Two question-mark tags swing over the skeletons.
shots.anim: Two question-mark tags swing on strings above them; a ticking clock SFX gives the viewer a beat to guess.

shots.vo: Most people pick the strong one as the farmer. Stored grain, a roof, tools. Surely that is the better life.
shots.visual: A viewer-like character in a museum points confidently at skeleton A.
shots.anim: A museum visitor walks in (walk cycle) and points confidently at A; small smug nod.

shots.vo: It's the other way round. The tall, healthy skeleton was the hunter-gatherer. The worn-out one was the farmer.
shots.visual: Tags flip: A gets 'HUNTER-GATHERER', B gets 'FARMER'. Gentle stamp sound.
shots.anim: The tags flip over like cards (scaleX through 0); a soft stamp SFX on each.

shots.vo: And it isn't one odd pair. In study after study, where farming took over, average height dropped and tooth decay, worn joints and signs of hunger went up.
shots.visual: Simple bar chart: average height before and after farming, plus three icons (tooth, spine, hunger lines) rising.
shots.anim: Bars drop on 'height dropped'; tooth, spine and hunger icons rise one by one; ink-line chart style.

shots.vo: In parts of Greece and Turkey, men's average height fell by around fifteen centimetres after farming arrived, and took thousands of years to come back.
shots.visual: Two painted men stand back to back with a height marker between them; the gap is highlighted.
shots.anim: Two men stand back to back; a height marker slides up between them and the gap highlights red.

shots.vo: A skeleton works like a diary. It records how you ate, how you moved and how hard you worked, and it keeps that record for thousands of years.
shots.visual: Bones fade into a leather diary; pages turn, each page a sketch of a body at work.
shots.anim: Bones dissolve into a leather diary; pages turn on their own (paper SFX), each page a sketch of a body at work.

shots.vo: And those diaries say the people with only spears were, in many ways, better fed and less worn down than the farmers who came after them.
shots.visual: Diary page shows the hunter's camp, warm; the next page shows a bent farmer in a field, grey.
shots.anim: Diary page left warm and colourful, page turn to the grey bent farmer; the colour drains as the page turns.

shots.vo: But bones can't tell you what an ordinary day felt like. For that, we need to walk through one.
shots.visual: Push in on the hunter page until it becomes the next scene.
shots.anim: Camera pushes into the hunter page until it fills the frame and becomes the next scene (match cut).

acts.name: Act 2: A Day Without a Clock

shots.vo: You wake at first light, on your own, because you slept enough.
shots.visual: Dawn camp: grass shelters, sleeping hides, low fire; mist on the plain.
shots.anim: Dawn camp, mist drifting; slow pan right across shelters; a sleeper turns over and sits up on his own.

shots.vo: Last night's fire is still alive. People sit around it, eating leftover meat and nuts.
shots.visual: Group of six around the fire, eating; steam rises; small kids lean on adults.
shots.anim: Six people eat around the fire; hands to mouths on staggered timers; steam rises; a child leans on an adult.

shots.vo: The talk is simple: where the water is good, where someone saw fresh tracks. That is the whole plan for the day, and everyone has a say in it.
shots.visual: Elder draws a map in the dirt with a stick; others lean in and point.
shots.anim: The elder draws a map in the dirt with a stick (line draws on); others lean in and point; heads turn to whoever speaks.

shots.vo: Today, nobody needs to hunt. The last kill was two days ago, and there is still food.
shots.visual: Calendar-style tally carved on a stick: two notches since the last hunt.
shots.anim: Notches carve themselves into a stick one by one (scrape SFX).

shots.vo: A few people walk out to gather roots, nuts and berries.
shots.visual: Two women and a teenager walk into the bush with digging sticks and carrying bags, walking cycle with distance covered.
shots.anim: Three gatherers walk out into the bush with digging sticks; real walk cycle covering ground; they shrink into the distance.

shots.vo: You stay and work on your gear. You sharpen a spear point. You work a stiff hide until it turns soft.
shots.visual: Close shots of hands knapping stone and scraping a pegged-out hide; 3D spear and hide props.
shots.anim: Close shots: hands knapping stone (chip SFX, sparks of flake), then scraping the pegged hide in rhythm.

shots.vo: Not because a boss told you to. Here, skill earns respect, and respect is worth more than anything you could own.
shots.visual: Others glance over admiringly at the finished spear point.
shots.anim: Others glance over; one nods; a small smile; the spear point catches the light.

shots.vo: By early afternoon, the jobs that needed doing are done.
shots.visual: Sun higher; the gatherers return with full bags; tools laid out finished. Hours clock shows a big free block.
shots.anim: Sun shadow swings (time passes). Gatherers return with full bags. Hours clock fills with a large free block (tick SFX).

acts.name: Act 3: The Hunter Who Never Stops

shots.vo: Two days later, the meat runs low. Today you hunt.
shots.visual: Morning: three hunters set out across a wide hot plain carrying spears and water gourds.
shots.anim: Three hunters set out across a hot plain, walk cycles in step; heat shimmer distortion on the horizon.

shots.vo: Some hunters in Africa have been recorded using a method that looks nothing like the movies. They don't try to outrun the animal. They can't.
shots.visual: A kudu bolts away; the hunters don't sprint, they keep a steady jog.
shots.anim: The kudu bolts away fast (animal run cycle); the hunters keep an even jog; dust kicks up.

shots.vo: Instead they track it, at a steady pace, for hours, in the midday heat.
shots.visual: Footprints in sand; hunters read the tracks, then jog on; sun high and harsh.
shots.anim: Close on footprints in the sand; a hand touches a track; then they jog on; sun high and harsh.

shots.vo: A human can sweat and keep cooling while moving. A four-legged runner has to stop to pant. Push it hard enough, for long enough, and it overheats.
shots.visual: Side-by-side thermometer graphic: human steady, antelope climbing into red.
shots.anim: Two thermometers: the human line stays level, the antelope's climbs into red with a warning pulse.

shots.vo: Eventually the animal stops and can't run again. The hunters walk up to it.
shots.visual: Long shot: the kudu stands still under a lone tree; hunters approach slowly. Non-graphic; cut away before the kill.
shots.anim: Long shot: the kudu stands still under a lone tree; hunters approach slowly. Cut away before any kill.

shots.vo: You were never the fastest thing on the plain. You were the thing that could keep going.
shots.visual: Silhouette of the hunter against the sun, breathing hard but steady.
shots.anim: Silhouette against the sun; chest heaving slowly; low heartbeat SFX; slow push-in.

shots.vo: This is called persistence hunting, and it's only one method among many. Most hunts used traps, snares, ambush and poisoned arrows.
shots.visual: Quick montage card: snare, bow with arrows, ambush behind a bush.
shots.anim: Three small vignettes pop in left to right on each word.

shots.vo: A big hunt can take the whole day, and it's the hardest work this life asks for. But one good kill feeds the camp for days.
shots.visual: Hunters return at dusk carrying meat; the camp gathers; fire built up.
shots.anim: Dusk: hunters return carrying meat; the camp stands to greet them; the fire is built up and flares.

shots.vo: So tomorrow, the free time comes back.
shots.visual: Hours clock fills back up with a free afternoon.
shots.anim: The hours clock refills with a free afternoon block (soft chime).

acts.name: Act 4: The Man With the Stopwatch

shots.vo: If this sounds too easy, you're not the first to think so. In 1963, a young anthropologist had the same doubt.
shots.visual: Sepia 1960s look: a young researcher with a notebook steps off a Land Rover.
shots.anim: Sepia 1960s grade. A Land Rover rolls in and stops (eased); the researcher steps out with a notebook.

shots.vo: His name was Richard Lee. He went to the Dobe area on the edge of the Kalahari, in Botswana.
shots.visual: Map of southern Africa; the Kalahari shaded; a pin on Dobe near the Namibia border.
shots.anim: Map of southern Africa; Kalahari shades in; pin drops on Dobe near the Namibia border.

shots.vo: He lived with the Ju/'hoansi, people who at the time still lived largely by hunting and gathering.
shots.visual: Painted Kalahari camp: grass huts, mongongo trees, dry sand; the researcher sits apart, writing.
shots.anim: Painted Kalahari camp, mongongo trees; the researcher sits apart, writing; camp life moves around him.

shots.vo: The textbook story said life like this meant working every daylight hour just to survive. Lee decided not to assume it. He counted it.
shots.visual: Notebook pages fill with tally marks; a stopwatch ticks.
shots.anim: Tally marks write themselves into the notebook; the stopwatch hand sweeps (tick SFX).

shots.vo: For weeks, he recorded who went out for food, for how long, and what they brought back.
shots.visual: Montage: Lee follows a gatherer, notes times, weighs nuts on a hanging scale.
shots.anim: Lee follows a gatherer (two walk cycles); nuts tip onto a hanging scale that swings and settles.

shots.vo: The result surprised everyone. Finding food took adults about fifteen hours a week. Roughly two and a half days.
shots.visual: Big number reveal over a week calendar: 15 HRS highlighted across Mon-Wed.
shots.anim: A week calendar; 15 hours shade in across Mon to Wed; the big number counts up 0 to 15.

shots.vo: If you work a normal job, you pass fifteen hours by Tuesday afternoon.
shots.visual: Office clock on Tuesday, 3 pm; the hours clock in the corner tips into overtime.
shots.anim: Office wall clock spins fast to Tuesday 3 pm; the hours clock in the corner tips into red.

shots.vo: To be fair, that number is only food. When Lee later added tool-making, cracking nuts, cooking and chores, the total rose to around forty hours a week.
shots.visual: Calendar adds stacked bars: food, tools, processing, chores; the total climbs to ~40.
shots.anim: Stacked bars add layer by layer: food, tools, processing, chores; total climbs to about 40.

shots.vo: That's close to a modern full-time job. But the shape was completely different. No commute, no fixed shift, no boss, and the work happened with family and friends around you.
shots.visual: Split frame: Ju/'hoan woman cracking nuts while chatting with friends vs. office worker alone in a cubicle.
shots.anim: Split: left, friends cracking nuts and laughing (talk mouths); right, one worker alone typing. Same clock on both sides.

shots.vo: Researchers later studied other foraging groups: the Hadza in Tanzania, the Aché in Paraguay, the Martu in Australia. The numbers vary a lot. Some groups spend far longer finding food.
shots.visual: World map with three pins lighting up in turn, each with a small hours bar of different length.
shots.anim: World map; three pins light in turn, each with a small bar of different length growing beside it.

shots.vo: So the real lesson isn't a magic number. It's who owned the hours. They decided when to work, how hard, and when to stop.
shots.visual: The hours clock changes label to 'HOURS THAT ARE YOURS'.
shots.anim: The corner clock moves to centre and grows; its label rewrites to HOURS THAT ARE YOURS.

shots.vo: Back at camp, it's afternoon, and the pace slows down.
shots.visual: Shaded camp under a big tree; light dapples; people lounge.
shots.anim: Dappled light moves through the big tree; people lounge; slow drift camera.

shots.vo: People sit in the shade and talk. Kids play. Someone combs through a friend's hair while the conversation wanders.
shots.visual: Several moving vignettes: kids playing with a hoop, two women chatting, an old man laughing.
shots.anim: Kids chase a hoop (run cycles); two women talk (mouths animate); an old man laughs (shoulders bounce).

shots.vo: Someone is drilling tiny holes through small shells, to string them as a necklace.
shots.visual: Close-up hands with a stone awl drilling a shell; 3D shell beads.
shots.anim: Close on hands drilling a tiny shell with a stone awl, twisting back and forth; shell dust puffs.

shots.vo: We know people did this, because at Blombos Cave in South Africa, archaeologists found shell beads about seventy-five thousand years old.
shots.visual: Map of South Africa's southern coast; Blombos Cave pin; then a painted cave mouth above the sea.
shots.anim: Map of the southern Cape; pin drops; dissolve to a painted cave mouth above the sea with waves rolling.

shots.vo: Dozens of tiny snail shells, each pierced and worn smooth where a string rubbed against it. Some were brought from river mouths kilometres away.
shots.visual: 3D row of Nassarius shell beads rotates, wear marks highlighted.
shots.anim: 3D row of shell beads rotates; wear marks highlight with small circles.

shots.vo: Gathered, carried home and drilled by hand. Not to eat. Just to look good.
shots.visual: A young woman ties the finished necklace on and smiles.
shots.anim: She ties the necklace on and smiles; beads catch the light.

shots.vo: And in 2008, in Hohle Fels cave in Germany, researchers pieced together a flute carved from a vulture's wing bone.
shots.visual: Map of Europe; a pin in south-west Germany; snowy Ice Age landscape plate.
shots.anim: Map of Europe to snowy Ice Age plate; snow falls; pin on south-west Germany.

shots.vo: It's around forty thousand years old, and it has five finger holes.
shots.visual: 3D bone flute rotates; the five holes glow one by one with a soft note each.
shots.anim: The bone flute rotates; its five holes glow one by one, each with a soft flute note.

shots.vo: Someone in the Ice Age made an instrument. Someone else had the time to learn to play it.
shots.visual: Ice Age musician plays by a fire; others listen; breath visible in the cold.
shots.anim: Ice Age musician plays by the fire, fingers lifting; listeners sway; breath visible in the cold.

shots.vo: Now think about what kept you alive here. No money. No police. No hospital.
shots.visual: Camp scene desaturates slightly; icons of money, a police badge and a hospital cross appear and get crossed out.
shots.onscreen: NO MONEY · NO POLICE · NO HOSPITAL
shots.anim: Camp desaturates; three icons appear and each is struck out with an ink X.

shots.vo: If your hunt fails, or you break a leg and can't walk for a month, the only safety net is other people.
shots.visual: An injured man sits with his leg bound; others bring him food.
shots.anim: An injured man with a bound leg; someone walks up and hands him food; he nods.

shots.vo: If people like you, they feed you. If they don't, nobody owes you anything.
shots.visual: Close on the food being handed over.
shots.anim: Close on the hand-over of food; warm light.

shots.vo: So those slow afternoons of talking and joking weren't wasted. They were insurance. Friendships were your bank, your hospital and your pension, all at once.
shots.visual: Three labels attach to the circle of people: BANK, HOSPITAL, PENSION.
shots.anim: Circle of people; three labels (BANK, HOSPITAL, PENSION) attach with lines and pop in.

shots.vo: Then the sun goes down, and the best part of the day begins.
shots.visual: Time-lapse sunset over the Kalahari; the fire is built up; sparks rise.
shots.anim: Time-lapse sunset: sky colour shifts warm to deep blue; the fire is built up and sparks rise.

shots.vo: In 2014, anthropologist Polly Wiessner published a study of how Ju/'hoan conversation changes after dark.
shots.visual: Researcher at a desk with old notebooks and a recorder; then the paper title card.
shots.anim: Researcher at a desk with old notebooks and a tape recorder; the paper's title card slides in.

shots.vo: She had notes and recordings gathered over decades, and she split them into two piles: talk by day, and talk by firelight.
shots.visual: Two piles of cards slide apart: a sun icon and a fire icon.
shots.anim: A pile of cards splits into two piles sliding apart under sun and fire icons.

shots.vo: Daytime talk was practical. Food, tracks, money and trade, and a lot of complaining and gossip about who wasn't sharing.
shots.visual: Daytime pie chart: work talk, complaints and gossip, jokes.
shots.anim: Daytime pie draws on clockwise: work talk, complaints and gossip, jokes.

shots.vo: By the fire, it changed. In the long night conversations, eighty-one percent were stories.
shots.visual: Night pie fills to 81% in firelight orange.
shots.anim: Night pie fills to 81% in firelight orange; number counts up.

shots.vo: Stories about ancestors, about how the world began, about people far away. Long jokes that ran deep into the night.
shots.visual: Firelit faces; shadows on the rocks behind form the story: ancestors, animals, stars.
shots.anim: Firelit faces; shadows on the rock wall behind act out the story (ancestors, animals, stars).

shots.vo: Wiessner argued that these firelit hours helped build what makes us human: shared memory, imagination and trust in people beyond the camp.
shots.visual: Embers rise into the stars, forming faint constellations.
shots.anim: Embers rise into the sky and join into faint constellations; camera tilts up with them.

shots.vo: Not in the middle of the work, but in the calm after it.
shots.visual: Slow push into the fire.
shots.anim: Slow push into the fire; crackle SFX up.

shots.vo: When the fire burns low, people sleep. But maybe not the way you do.
shots.visual: Moonlit camp; figures asleep under hides; embers glow.
shots.anim: Moonlit camp; sleepers breathe; embers glow and fade.

shots.vo: Historian Roger Ekirch found hundreds of old European records that mention a first sleep and a second sleep, with a waking hour in between.
shots.visual: Old parchment documents with highlighted phrases 'first sleep' and 'second sleep'; candlelight.
shots.anim: Candlelit parchment; the phrases highlight as if underlined by hand.

shots.vo: People would wake around midnight, lie quietly, think, pray or talk, and then sleep again.
shots.visual: A medieval couple wakes by candlelight and talks softly, then lies back down.
shots.anim: A medieval couple wakes by candle, talks softly, then lies back down; the candle flickers.

shots.vo: And when a 1990s experiment kept volunteers in long winter nights with no artificial light, many slipped into the same split pattern.
shots.visual: Two sleep blocks on a night timeline with a gap in the middle.
shots.anim: A night timeline draws left to right: sleep block, gap, sleep block.

shots.vo: Not every study agrees. When researchers tracked sleep among the Hadza, the San and the Tsimane, most slept in one block.
shots.visual: Card with three group names and a single solid sleep bar.
shots.anim: A card with three group names slides in; a single solid sleep bar draws under it.

shots.vo: So if you wake at two in the morning, it may not be a disorder. Your body may just be doing something very old.
shots.visual: Modern bedroom: phone shows 2:00; the figure lies calmly instead of panicking.
shots.anim: Modern bedroom; phone glows 2:00; he lies calmly, breathing; no panic.

shots.vo: That was the human rhythm for a very long time. Food in the morning, people in the afternoon, stories at night.
shots.visual: Montage of the three earlier moments across one painted panorama; the hours clock is mostly free.
shots.anim: A long panorama of the three earlier moments; camera pans across it; the hours clock is mostly free.

shots.vo: Then, roughly twelve thousand years ago, in the Fertile Crescent, people began planting wild grains and keeping animals.
shots.visual: Map of the Fertile Crescent arc lighting up green from the Levant to the Tigris and Euphrates.
shots.anim: The crescent arc lights green from the Levant to the Tigris and Euphrates.

shots.vo: On paper, it looked like an upgrade. More food. More control. No more tracking an antelope across the plain.
shots.visual: First farmer scatters seed; neat field rows appear; a pen of goats.
shots.anim: First farmer scatters seed (arm sweep); field rows draw in behind; goats in a pen.

shots.vo: But it set off a loop. More food meant more children survived. More people needed more food. More food meant more fields, and more fields meant more work.
shots.visual: Circular diagram, each arrow lighting as spoken: FOOD → PEOPLE → FIELDS → WORK → FOOD.
shots.anim: The loop's arrows light one after another as each word is said, then spin faster.

shots.vo: And then the door shut. Once a village grew too big to live off wild food, there was no going back.
shots.visual: A wooden gate swings shut on the field; the forest behind it fades.
shots.anim: A wooden gate swings shut (creak + thud); the forest behind it fades out.

shots.vo: Ploughing, sowing, weeding, harvesting, grinding, storing and guarding. Every season, every year.
shots.visual: Rapid cycle of farming tasks with the same bent figure; 3D plough and grain sacks; ambient wind.
shots.anim: Fast cycle of tasks with the same bent figure: plough, sow, weed, harvest, grind; wind ambience.

shots.vo: Remember the second skeleton? The decay, the worn spine, the shorter life. This is where it came from.
shots.visual: Skeleton B fades in over the bent farmer.
shots.anim: Skeleton B fades in over the bent farmer (double exposure).

shots.vo: Villages became towns. Towns needed potters, weavers and traders. Then cities, and with them kings, soldiers, priests and tax collectors.
shots.visual: A painted village grows in time-lapse into a walled city; figures appear in turn.
shots.anim: Time-lapse: huts become houses become a walled city; potters, a king, soldiers, a tax collector appear in turn.

shots.vo: And something new arrived in human history: hours that belonged to someone else, sold in exchange for food you no longer knew how to find.
shots.visual: A coin is placed in a farmer's hand; his hours clock is handed to a tax collector.
shots.anim: A coin drops into the farmer's hand; his hours clock floats across to the tax collector.

shots.vo: Nobody stole our time in one night. It was traded away slowly, over hundreds of generations, in a deal none of us got to vote on.
shots.visual: Generations pass: the same field, faces change, the city wall grows behind.
shots.anim: Generations pass in place: the same field, faces change, the city wall grows behind them.

shots.vo: And the alarm that woke you this morning is just the latest payment.
shots.visual: The modern phone alarm again, 6:00, cold light.
shots.anim: Back to the phone alarm, cold light; it rings (alarm SFX, shorter).

shots.vo: For most of human history, finding food took part of the week. Afternoons went to craft, beauty and friendship. Nights went to stories.
shots.visual: Recap panorama: hunt, shells and flute, the fire.
shots.anim: Recap panorama; quick parallax pan across hunt, shells and flute, the fire.

shots.vo: You will spend something like ninety thousand hours of your life at work.
shots.visual: Office tower at night, windows lit; the number counts up.
shots.anim: Office tower at night, windows lit; the number counts up.

shots.vo: We make art if there's anything left after the job. They made it on an ordinary afternoon.
shots.visual: Split: tired worker sketching at midnight / the shell necklace being made in daylight.
shots.anim: Split: tired worker sketching at midnight / the necklace being made in daylight.

shots.vo: We network to get ahead. They spent hours with the people they loved, and it counted as survival.
shots.visual: Split: business card exchange / grooming and laughing in the shade.
shots.anim: Split: two suits swap business cards / friends grooming and laughing in the shade.

shots.vo: We chase a finish line called retirement, where we finally get our time back.
shots.visual: A finish-line ribbon far down a long road of desks.
shots.anim: A road of desks recedes to a finish-line ribbon far away.

shots.vo: In one way, they were already standing on it.
shots.visual: Pull back: the hunter sits on the finish line by his fire, relaxed.
shots.anim: Pull back: the hunter is already sitting on the finish line by his fire, relaxed.

shots.vo: They woke up without an alarm, and asked the question you rarely get to ask.
shots.visual: Dawn again; the hunter stretches, looks out across the plain.
shots.anim: Dawn again; he stretches and looks out; the card from the cold open returns (bookend).

shots.vo: If this changed how you see your own day, watch next how farming built the first cities.
shots.visual: End card over the fire with the channel name.
shots.anim: End card over the fire; channel name; music resolves.

hooks: Your alarm went off this morning and your day stopped being yours. In 1963 a scientist timed people who still hunt and gather: 15 hours a week to find food. What are you paying for the other 25?
Everyone says cavemen worked every waking hour just to survive. You are the one who does. In 1963 a man with a stopwatch timed hunters: 15 hours a week.

titles: They Found Food in 15 Hours a Week. Where Did Your Time Go?
What Did Ancient Humans Actually Do All Day?
How Farming Stole Your Free Time

fixes: '17 hours a week' (transcript): Lee's 1960s food-getting figure is usually cited as about 12 to 19, average about 15 hours a week. Script uses ~15 and calls it food only.
Transcript leaves out that Lee's later total, adding tool-making, food processing and chores, was about 40 to 44 hours a week. Added, so the video isn't misleading.
'Hadza, Aché, Martu all came back 15 to 20 hours' is not supported: Aché men spent much longer hunting. Script says the numbers vary and some groups spend far longer.
'Lives than' (missing word) rewritten: 'better fed and less worn down'.
Skeleton height: cited as about 15 cm fall in men's average height in Greece/Turkey after farming (Angel 1984). Said 'in parts of', not 'everywhere'.
Blombos beads: about 75,000 years old (transcript said 'over 70,000'); shells came from estuaries some kilometres away, not 'a long walk to the coast'.
Hohle Fels flute: vulture wing bone, five finger holes, about 35,000 to 40,000 years old; found 2008. Kept as 'around forty thousand'.
'James Suzman: 6 hours a day of social time': couldn't find a source. Dropped.
Wiessner (PNAS 2014): 81% of long night-time conversations were stories. Correct; the name is spelled Wiessner (transcript had 'Weisner').
Two sleeps: historical European records (Ekirch) and the 1992 Wehr experiment support it, but Yetish et al. 2015 found Hadza, San and Tsimane mostly sleep in one block. Added the caveat.
Persistence hunting: presented as one documented method among many, not how all hunting worked.
Farming start: about 12,000 years ago in the Fertile Crescent (transcript said 10,000).
cuts: No sponsor segment in this transcript.
Unsourced 'Suzman 6 hours of social time a day' claim removed.
